literal: Zhen's younger brother Daba was enfeoffed as Baron of Julu.
idiomatic: Zhen's younger brother Daba was made Baron of Julu.

literal: Daba's grandson Bao, style Daocheng, was plain and honest and loved reading.
idiomatic: Daba's grandson Bao, styled Daocheng, was plain, honest, and fond of books.

literal: In Emperor Ming's time he served to Governor of Shuozhou.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he rose to governor of Shuozhou.

literal: Border affairs flared repeatedly and many people were displaced.
idiomatic: Border wars drove many into flight.

literal: When Bao arrived, he gradually brought them back and settled them.
idiomatic: When Bao arrived he gradually gathered and settled them.

literal: Ruined old dwellings—he ordered them all repaired;
idiomatic: Ruined houses he ordered rebuilt;

literal: people returned in an unbroken stream, and his yearly assessment ranked first in the realm.
idiomatic: refugees returned in streams, and his yearly rating ranked first in the realm.

literal: Later he followed the Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong in attacking Ge Rong.
idiomatic: Later he followed Grand Commander Yuan Ziyong against Ge Rong.

literal: The imperial army suffered defeat.
idiomatic: The imperial army was routed.

literal: Bao was taken prisoner in Rong's army; he changed his name, hid among the soldiers, and escaped harm.
idiomatic: Bao was taken by Rong's army; he changed his name, hid among the ranks, and survived.

literal: A long time passed.
idiomatic: A long time passed.

literal: Among the rebels a man of Shuozhou recognized Bao and said to him, "My lord, would you truly torment yourself to this point?
idiomatic: A Shuozhou man among the rebels knew him and said, "My lord, must you suffer so?

literal: He was therefore taken to Rong.
idiomatic: They took him to Rong.

literal: Rong laughed and said, "Master Lou, I am just now plotting affairs—how late you come to see me!
idiomatic: Rong laughed: "Master Lou, I am plotting great things—how late you come!

literal: He then turned and told others, "This gentleman does good; heaven rewards him—escaping the marauders is proof."
idiomatic: He told his men, "This man does good; heaven spared him from the mob—that is proof."

literal: When Bao met fugitives he secretly reported the rebels' situation and plotted to act as an inside agent.
idiomatic: Bao secretly sent word on rebel strength through fugitives and plotted as an inside man.

literal: The Son of Heaven was moved by his stalwart will and summoned Bao's second son Jingxian, appointing him Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: The emperor, moved by his courage, summoned Bao's second son Jingxian and made him Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

literal: When Ge Rong was destroyed, Bao at last returned.
idiomatic: When Ge Rong fell, Bao at last came home.

literal: In the Yongan era he was made Acting Supernumerary Regular Attendant and sent to the Rouran.
idiomatic: In Yongan he was made Acting Supernumerary Regular Attendant and sent to the Rouran.

literal: Earlier the Rouran had called themselves vassals and submitted a memorial, but later, seeing the central provinces in disorder, they wrote in the forms of a hostile state.
idiomatic: The Rouran had once submitted as vassals, but later, seeing the central lands in turmoil, wrote as to an equal enemy.

literal: Bao rebuked them.
idiomatic: Bao rebuked them.

literal: The Rouran ruler was greatly alarmed, knew himself in the wrong, and apologized, saying, "The scribe who drafted this letter erred."
idiomatic: The Rouran ruler was alarmed, confessed fault, and said the letter was a clerk's mistake.

literal: They then again called themselves vassals.
idiomatic: They again styled themselves vassals.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was enthroned, an edict ordered Bao and Field Secretariat Chief Zhangsun Ziyan to garrison Hengnong.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu rose, Bao and Field Secretariat Chief Zhangsun Ziyan were ordered to hold Hengnong.

literal: Later he followed the court into Guanzhong and was enfeoffed Baron of Guangning.
idiomatic: He followed the court into Guanzhong and was made Baron of Guangning.

literal: In the first year of Datong, an edict put him in charge of the Director of Literature, overseeing the compilation of the national history, with a separate enfeoffment as Baron of Pingcheng.
idiomatic: In Datong 1 he was put over the Director of Literature to oversee the national history and enfeoffed Baron of Pingcheng.

literal: Later he was made Director of the National University, Palace Attendant, advanced to Pillar of State, concurrently Tutor of the Crown Prince, and acting Supervisor of the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: Later he became Director of the National University, Palace Attendant, Pillar of State, Tutor of the Crown Prince, and acting Supervisor of the Eastern Palace.

literal: Bao as a man was pure, sparing of words, and well versed in old affairs.
idiomatic: Bao was spare of speech, pure in manner, and versed in precedent.

literal: His posts were those of a teacher; he kept to quiet respect and was therefore honored by others.
idiomatic: He held the posts of a teacher and kept quiet respect, and men honored him.

literal: Later he administered Jing Province and died in office.
idiomatic: Later he administered Jing Province and died there.

literal: Lu Dafei, a man of the Rouran.
idiomatic: Lu Dafei was a Rouran.

literal: In Emperor Daowu's time he came over to Wei, married Princess Huayang, and was enfeoffed Baron of Qisi.
idiomatic: In Daowu's time he submitted to Wei, married Princess Huayang, and was made Baron of Qisi.

literal: With his younger brother he became a senior guest and entered the Eight Deliberations.
idiomatic: He and his brother became senior guests and entered the Eight Deliberations.

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, he was made Grand Officer of the Inner Capital and advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne he was made Grand Officer of the Inner Capital and raised to marquis.

literal: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin attacked Wulao, Dafei and E Qing led twelve armies on the middle route.
idiomatic: When Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin attacked Wulao, Dafei and E Qing led twelve armies on the center road.

literal: In early Taiwu he again campaigned with Xi Jin by the White Road from Yunzhong against Da Tan and defeated him.
idiomatic: Early in Taiwu he again marched with Xi Jin from Yunzhong by the White Road against Da Tan and defeated him.

literal: Later he followed the campaign against He Lian Chang and for merit was made Duke of Xingyang.
idiomatic: He followed the campaign against He Lian Chang and was made Duke of Xingyang.

literal: When the princess died, he again married Princess Huzhe.
idiomatic: When his princess died he married Princess Huzhe.

literal: Taiwu was about to enfeoff Dafei as king when he fell ill and died.
idiomatic: Taiwu was about to make him a king when illness took him.

literal: Xi Mu, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Xi Mu was from Dai.

literal: Heavy, steady, and full of stratagem, Daowu favored him and called him Second Brother.
idiomatic: Steady and resourceful, Daowu favored him and called him Second Brother.

literal: Earlier, when Liu Xian harmed the emperor, Liang Juan knew it and secretly sent Mu with Mu Chong to Seven Mountains to report.
idiomatic: When Liu Xian harmed the emperor, Liang Juan knew and secretly sent Mu with Mu Chong to Seven Mountains to warn Daowu.

literal: The emperor recorded the old ministers of the former emperor; because Mu had reported Xian's deed, he was made to present memorials on government and join in planning.
idiomatic: Daowu honored old service and, for Mu's warning of Xian, set him to memorials and counsel.

literal: In the campaign against Murong Bao he was for merit made Governor of Bingzhou and enfeoffed Duke of Rencheng.
idiomatic: Against Murong Bao he was made governor of Bingzhou and Duke of Rencheng.

literal: The province bordered Yao Xing, and Xing often raided the frontier.
idiomatic: Bingzhou bordered Yao Xing, who often raided.

literal: Mu then wrote Xing, styling himself with bowed head yet matching him in ritual, rebuking Xing's unjust border raids.
idiomatic: Mu wrote Xing, bowing his head in form yet matching him in rank, and rebuked his raids.

literal: Xing, wishing peace with the state, resented it and spoke to Daowu; Daowu executed Mu.
idiomatic: Xing, wanting peace, complained to Daowu, and Daowu had Mu executed.

literal: He Ba, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: He Ba was from Dai.

literal: For generations his line led their tribe as Wei's attached subjects.
idiomatic: His line had led their tribe as Wei subjects for generations.

literal: At Ba's time he was famed for talent and eloquence.
idiomatic: In Ba's time he was famed for eloquence and wit.

literal: Daowu promoted him to senior minister of the outer court, joining in great state counsel; he had elegant wisdom and calculation and was enfeoffed Duke of Rinan.
idiomatic: Daowu made him a senior outer-court minister in great counsel; he was enfeoffed Duke of Rinan.

literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, for merit he was advanced to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and garrisoned Ye.
idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and held Ye.

literal: For defeating Murong De's army he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Dingling.
idiomatic: For breaking Murong De's army he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Dingling.

literal: With Prince of Changshan Zun he attacked the Helan splinter chieftain Muyiqian and defeated him.
idiomatic: With Prince of Changshan Zun he defeated the Helan splinter chief Muyiqian.

literal: He went out as Administrator of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Pingyuan.

literal: Daowu favored Ba above the other generals.
idiomatic: Daowu favored Ba above other generals.

literal: The ministers all prized respectful frugality, but Ba loved to cultivate empty reputation and dazzle the age.
idiomatic: Ministers prized frugality; Ba courted empty fame and dazzled his age.

literal: His nature was especially extravagant and dissolute; the emperor admonished him but he did not reform.
idiomatic: He was extravagant; the emperor warned him in vain.

literal: Later, when the imperial carriage hunted north at Mount Shi, Ba was arrested and executed by the roadside.
idiomatic: Later, on a northern hunt at Mount Shi, Ba was seized and executed by the road.

literal: His wife Lady Liu killed herself to follow him.
idiomatic: His wife Lady Liu killed herself to follow.

literal: When Ba was first to be executed, Daowu ordered his younger brothers Pi and others to witness the farewell.
idiomatic: Before the execution Daowu ordered his brothers Pi and others to witness his farewell.

literal: Ba told Pi, "The land north of the Luo is poor; you may settle south of the water, take good fields in cultivation, broaden your estates, and urge one another on."
idiomatic: Ba told Pi, "North of the Luo the land is poor—settle south of the river, till good fields, and build your estates."

literal: Turning his back on them he said, "How can you bear to watch my death!
idiomatic: Turning away he cried, "How can you bear to watch me die!

literal: Pi and the others grasped his subtle intent, falsely claimed to be envoys, and fled to Chang'an.
idiomatic: Pi and the others read his hint, pretended to be envoys, and fled to Chang'an.

literal: Daowu exterminated his family.
idiomatic: Daowu exterminated his family.

literal: Later, when Emperor Taiwu hunted at Mount Shi, sudden thick fog closed in on every side; in wonder he asked the cause.
idiomatic: Later Taiwu hunted at Mount Shi; sudden fog closed every side, and he asked why.

literal: The crowd all said Ba had dwelt here and his shrine tomb still stood—perhaps he could bring such change.
idiomatic: All said Ba had lived there and his tomb still stood—perhaps he caused it.

literal: The emperor sent Duke of Jianxing Gu Bi to sacrifice with the three beasts; the fog at once lifted.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Duke of Jianxing Gu Bi with the triple offering; the fog lifted.

literal: Afterward, on every day of Taiwu's hunts, he first sent men to sacrifice to him.
idiomatic: Afterward, on every hunt, Taiwu first sent sacrifice to Ba.

literal: Mo Ti, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Mo Ti was from Dai.

literal: Full of wisdom and able in office.
idiomatic: He was clever and capable.

literal: At first he was a standard-bearer general commanding the guard troops.
idiomatic: At first he was a standard-bearer general over the guard.

literal: In Daowu's campaign against Murong Bao, Bao attacked the camp by night and the army was alarmed.
idiomatic: When Daowu campaigned against Murong Bao, Bao raided the camp by night and the army panicked.

literal: Some fled back to the capital, saying the imperial army had been defeated at Baixi.
idiomatic: Some fled to the capital reporting defeat at Baixi.

literal: The capital was uneasy; the Western Pacification General Yuan Shun of Nan'an therefore meant to seize state affairs.
idiomatic: The capital shook; Nan'an's Yuan Shun meant to seize power.

literal: Ti said, "Great affairs must not be treated lightly—otherwise calamity will come!
idiomatic: Ti said, "Great affairs are not to be seized lightly—or disaster follows!

literal: Shun then stopped.
idiomatic: Shun then stopped.

literal: Later he was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoyi.
idiomatic: He was later made Duke of Gaoyi.

literal: When Kudou raided the southern marches, Ti at the time was disloyal to the emperor and sent Kudou an arrow, telling him, "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load!
idiomatic: When Kudou raided the south, Ti, then disloyal, sent him an arrow: "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load?

literal: The words meant Kudou was grown and the emperor still young.
idiomatic: He meant Kudou was grown and the emperor young.

literal: The emperor bore a grudge; later someone reported that Ti's bearing was arrogant and modeled on a ruler's.
idiomatic: The emperor remembered; later someone reported Ti's arrogance and princely bearing.

literal: The emperor then had men show him the arrow and tell him, "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load or not?
idiomatic: The emperor showed him the arrow and asked, "Can a three-year calf bear a heavy load?

literal: Ti received the edict; father and son wept facing each other.
idiomatic: Ti took the edict; father and son wept together.

literal: At the next court session he was executed.
idiomatic: At the next audience he was executed.

literal: He Digan, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: He Digan was from Dai.

literal: His family was originally of a small clan; for generations they were honest and steady, and as generals they were famed for fairness.
idiomatic: His clan was small and for generations honest; as a commander he was famed for fairness.

literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Chief of the Northern Tribes.
idiomatic: He rose to Grand Chief of the Northern Tribes.

literal: At the founding of the state he was paired with Zhangsun Song.
idiomatic: At the state's founding he was paired with Zhangsun Song.

literal: Clear in hearing and judgment, he was loved and respected by men.
idiomatic: Keen of ear and judgment, he was loved and respected.

literal: Daowu sent Digan to present a thousand horses and conclude a marriage with Yao Chang.
idiomatic: Daowu sent Digan with a thousand horses to seal marriage with Yao Chang.

literal: Chang died and Xing took the throne; he therefore detained Digan and broke the betrothal.
idiomatic: Chang died; Xing detained Digan and broke the match.

literal: Xing's younger brother Pingkou pacified Pingyang; Daowu campaigned, pacified him, and captured his generals Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and more than forty others.
idiomatic: Xing's brother Pingkou held Pingyang; Daowu defeated him and took Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, and forty more.

literal: Later Xing offered a thousand fine horses to ransom Bozhi and sent Digan back; the emperor permitted it.
idiomatic: Later Xing offered a thousand horses for Bozhi and returned Digan; the emperor agreed.

literal: While in Chang'an, Digan studied histories and mastered the Analects, Documents, and other classics; his bearing was elegant, like a Confucian's.
idiomatic: In Chang'an he studied histories and the Analects and Documents; his bearing grew elegant, like a scholar's.

literal: Earlier, when the emperor enfeoffed the meritous in general, though Digan was detained by Yao Xing, he was enfeoffed from afar as Marquis of Xiangwu and made General of Qin Troops.
idiomatic: When merit was rewarded, though Xing still held him, Digan was enfeoffed from afar as Marquis of Xiangwu and General of Qin Troops.

literal: When Digan arrived, the emperor saw his speech and dress resembled the central lands and thought he had admired and learned them; he was therefore angry and soon killed him.
idiomatic: When Digan returned, the emperor saw his speech and dress like the central lands, thought him a mimic, grew angry, and killed him.

literal: Li Li, a man of Yanmen.
idiomatic: Li Li was from Yanmen.

literal: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather entered the north.
idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's time his father and grandfather came north.

literal: Li in youth was eloquent and quick, with talent and also military stratagem.
idiomatic: Li in youth was quick and eloquent, gifted in arms as well as wit.

literal: At first he followed Daowu on his visit to the Helan; Daowu loved his arts.
idiomatic: At first he followed Daowu to the Helan; Daowu loved his skill.
